overview.text: The Urutu (Crossed Pit Viper) is a large, highly venomous pit viper of south-eastern South America and an important cause of snakebites there. Its name *alternatus* means 'alternating', for the staggered marks on its body.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Large and stout: usually 0.8 to 1.2 m; the longest verified was 1.69 m. Females are bigger.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: South-eastern Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay and northern and central Argentina.

habitat.text: Forests, but mostly damp places such as marshes, swamps and riversides; also sugarcane fields.

recognise.text: Staggered, curved dark marks along a heavy body.
